tasks.subject: T5: Mach-O undefined-symbol parser (with leading-underscore handling)
tasks.description:
Parse LC_SYMTAB; collect external undefined symbols (n_type & N_STAB == 0, (n_type & N_TYPE) == N_UNDF, n_type & N_EXT). CRITICAL: strip the leading underscore Mach-O prepends to C symbols BEFORE the numbox_pxy_ prefix test and the ll.address_of_symbol lookup, else the parser matches _numbox_pxy_ against numbox_pxy_ , finds nothing, and silently passes every stale object (the trap the portability verdict flagged). Handle 32/64-bit + both endiannesses via magic (0xFEEDFACE/0xFEEDFACF + byteswaps); handle fat/universal if numba emits it. Check in a small Mach-O fixture object carrying a numbox_pxy_* undefined symbol for a Linux-runnable unit test. Cannot be truly validated locally — final proof is the fork CI macos-latest job.


tasks.subject: T6: COFF/PE undefined-symbol parser (Windows)
tasks.description:
Parse the COFF symbol table at f_symptr with the string table immediately after; collect external undefined symbols (n_scnum == IMAGE_SYM_UNDEFINED (0) and n_sclass == IMAGE_SYM_CLASS_EXTERNAL); names are inline (8 bytes, NUL-padded) or a string-table offset (first 4 bytes zero). Confirm empirically whether x64 prepends a leading underscore (x64 __cdecl generally does not, unlike x86) rather than assuming. Check in a small COFF fixture for a Linux-runnable unit test. Final proof is the fork CI windows-latest job.
